q.t: Write 25% as a fraction in lowest terms.
q.e: Per cent means ‘out of 100’: 25/100. Divide top and bottom by 25 → 1/4.

q.t: Write 3/5 as a percentage.
q.e: Make the denominator 100: 3/5 = 60/100 = 60%.

q.t: Find 10% of 250.
q.e: 10% is one tenth, so divide by 10: 25.

q.t: Write 0.45 as a percentage.
q.e: 0.45 = 45 hundredths = 45 out of 100 = 45%. Multiply a decimal by 100 to get the percentage.

q.t: Find 50% of 80.
q.e: 50% is half, and half of 80 is 40.

q.t: Rohan scored 7 out of 20. What percentage is that?
q.e: 7/20 = 35/100 (multiply top and bottom by 5), so 35%.

q.t: Write 75% as a decimal.
Find 100% of 63.
q.e: 100% means 100 out of 100 — the whole thing.

q.t: Find 20% of ₹300 (in ₹).
q.e: 10% of 300 is 30, so 20% is double: 60.

q.t: What percent of 50 is 5?
Find 12.5% of 640.
36 is what percent of 150?
15% of a number is 45. Find the number.
Increase 80 by 25%.
Decrease 250 by 12%.
Write 2/3 as a percentage.
q.e: 2/3 × 100 = 200/3 = 66 2/3. It never comes out exactly, so keep the fraction.

q.t: What percent of a day is 1 hour 12 minutes?
q.e: Same units: 72 minutes out of 24 × 60 = 1440 minutes. 72/1440 = 1/20 = 5%.

q.t: 35% of a number is 84. Find the number.
Write 7.5% as a fraction in lowest terms.
In a class of 40 students, 15% are absent. How many are present?
q.e: Absent = 15% of 40 = 6. Present = 40 − 6 = 34. (Or 85% of 40.)

q.t: Meera scored 432 marks out of 600. What is her percentage?
A town of 25,000 people grows by 8% in a year. What is the new population?
The price of a bag falls from ₹800 to ₹680. What is the percentage decrease?
q.e: Decrease = 120. Percentage change is always measured on the ORIGINAL: 120/800 × 100 = 15%.

q.t: When 40% of a number is added to 42, the result is the number itself. Find the number.
q.e: 42 must be the missing 60% of the number. 60% → 42, so 100% → 70.

q.t: An alloy is 30% copper, 45% zinc and the rest nickel. How much nickel is in 800 g of the alloy (in g)?
A’s income is 25% more than B’s. By what percent is B’s income less than A’s?
q.e: Let B = 100, then A = 125. B is 25 less than A, measured on A: 25/125 = 20%. The base changed, so the percentage changes.

q.t: In a school 60% of the students are girls. There are 320 boys. How many students are there altogether?
q.e: Boys are the other 40%. 40% → 320, so 100% → 800.

q.t: A number is increased by 20% and the result is then decreased by 20%. Overall the number has:
q.e: Start with 100 → 120. Now 20% of 120 is 24 (not 20), giving 96. Net fall of 4%, because the second 20% is of a bigger number.

q.t: A town has 15,000 voters and 8% did not vote. How many votes were cast?
x% of 75 is 9. Find x.
In an election between two candidates, the winner got 58% of the votes and won by 2400 votes. How many votes were cast in all?
q.e: The loser got 42%. The gap is 58 − 42 = 16% of the votes = 2400, so 1% = 150 and 100% = 15,000.

q.t: The price of sugar rises by 25%. By what percent must a family cut the amount it buys so that it spends the same as before?
q.e: A ₹100 budget once bought 100 units; now each costs 1.25, so it buys 100 ÷ 1.25 = 80 units. That is a 20% cut.

q.t: A salary is raised by 10%, and then the new salary is raised by 10% again. What is the overall percentage increase?
q.e: 100 → 110 → 121. The second 10% is on 110, so it adds 11, giving 21% in all (not 20%).

q.t: 30% of 40% of a number is 48. Find the number.
A student needs 40% to pass. She scores 178 marks and fails by 22 marks. What are the maximum marks?
q.e: Pass mark = 178 + 22 = 200. That is 40% of the maximum, so maximum = 200 ÷ 0.4 = 500.

q.t: Each side of a square is increased by 10%. By what percent does its area increase?
q.e: Side 10 → 11. Area 100 → 121. Area grows by 21% because BOTH dimensions grow.

q.t: An ore contains 12% copper. How much ore is needed to get 69 kg of copper (in kg)?
q.e: 12% of the ore = 69 kg, so ore = 69 ÷ 0.12 = 575 kg.

q.t: A town of 20,000 people grows by 10% in the first year and shrinks by 10% in the second. What is the population after two years?
q.e: After year 1: 22,000. Year 2 loses 10% of 22,000 = 2,200, leaving 19,800.

q.t: A is 150% of B. What percent of (A + B) is B?
In a class, 70% passed in maths, 65% passed in science and 27% failed in both. What percent passed in both subjects?
q.e: Passed at least one = 100 − 27 = 73%. Adding 70 + 65 = 135 counts the ‘both’ group twice, so both = 135 − 73 = 62%.
